name: Nirvana
label: Sub Pop
lede: Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic recorded Bleach for $606.17, and three years later Nevermind was No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Cobain died in April 1994, seven years after the band's first show.

eras.title: Nameless in Aberdeen
eras.text: Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic met through the Melvins crowd in Aberdeen, Washington, a mill town two hours from Seattle. For a year the band had no fixed name and no fixed drummer, and a producer's tape, not a gig, got them noticed.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic and Aaron Burckhard, c. 1987
yt: Full audio of the Raymond house party, March 1987
years.h: Nirvana's first show is a house party in Raymond
years.p: Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic and drummer [[Aaron Burckhard|86d3f2c7-2a19-4249-ad7c-6feec74118d7]] play 17 Nussbaum Road in Raymond, Washington, and somebody tapes it.
years.xp:
The tape has the trio running through originals, restarting Hairspray Queen several times, along with Led Zeppelin's Heartbreaker and How Many More Times. At one point a voice says, "We do have a decent PA, it just keeps blowing up!"

Through 1987 the band played as Skid Row, Pen Cap Chew, Bliss and Ted Ed Fred. Burckhard was gone by the end of the year.

years.h: Melvins drummer Dale Crover sits in on a one-day demo
years.p: Cobain and Novoselic cut ten songs at [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]]'s Reciprocal Recording. Endino hands the tape to Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman.

years.h: Tacoma gets the first show billed as Nirvana
years.p: The band plays Community World Theater after a year of throwaway names.
years.xp: Cobain on the name: "I wanted a name that was kind of beautiful or nice and pretty instead of a mean, raunchy punk name."

years.h: Chad Channing becomes the drummer who stays
years.p: [[Chad Channing|e2f28104-72bb-4c8f-b0f9-78d4eaf492fd]], from Bainbridge Island, plays his first Nirvana show and holds the drum stool for two years.

years.h: Love Buzz goes out by mail
years.p: Nirvana's first single covers Shocking Blue and is Sub Pop Singles Club No. 1, a hand-numbered run of 1,000 for subscribers.

eras.title: The drummer who stuck came from D.C.
eras.text: Bleach made Nirvana a working Sub Pop band and sent them across Europe in a cramped van with Tad. By the end of 1990 they had tapes with Butch Vig, a drummer from Washington, D.C., and major labels calling.

yt: Live at the Pyramid Club, July 18, 1989
years.h: A $606.17 debut, paid for by a guitarist who never played on it
years.p: Recorded with Jack Endino at Reciprocal Recording over thirty hours, from Christmas Eve 1988 to January 24, 1989. About a Girl is Cobain's pop song among the sludge.
years.xp:
[[Jason Everman|797dc323-fc39-4597-98cc-d10493f67326]] heard the demo, put up the $606.17 and joined as second guitarist in February 1989. He's credited on the sleeve and pictured on the cover but plays nothing on it, and he's still on the cover of the 2009 reissue. Wikipedia puts the first run at about 40,000 copies.

Cobain later said of the sound: "There was this pressure from Sub Pop and the grunge scene to play 'rock music'." The cover photo was taken by his girlfriend then, Tracy Marander, at the Reko Muse gallery in Olympia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jason Everman · Revolver: How Jason Everman
years.h: Jason Everman leaves, and Soundgarden has him by fall
years.p: He's out after Nirvana's first U.S. tour. Everman has said he quit; Cobain said the band fired him.
years.xp: Everman filled in on bass for [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]] and was fired in 1990 over conflicts, particularly with Chris Cornell. He enlisted in the Army in September 1994, served with the 2nd Ranger Battalion and 3rd Special Forces Group in Afghanistan and Iraq, and finished a philosophy degree at Columbia in 2013.

years.h: Cobain climbs the PA mid-set in Rome
years.p: On a European tour with [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]], Cobain scales a speaker stack at a Rome show and threatens to jump, as Michael Azerrad tells it in Come as You Are.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain in a floral dress, Hampshire College, Amherst, Massachusetts, April 27, 1990
years.h: A tape from Madison does more than any release
years.p: Nirvana record songs for a second Sub Pop album with [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] at Smart Studios in Madison, Wisconsin. The tapes circulate among major labels.

years.h: Chad Channing walks out
years.p: He's frustrated at having little say in the songwriting. The band goes looking for a drummer who hits harder.

years.h: Sliver gets an hour, on a break from a Mudhoney session
years.p: Dan Peters of [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]] drums on the July 11 session at Reciprocal. It's Nirvana's last new release on Sub Pop.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain and the crowd, Motor Sports International Garage, Seattle, September 22, 1990
years.src: Wikipedia: Nirvana · Rolling Stone: Dave Grohl
years.h: Dave Grohl flies in after Scream collapses
years.p: When D.C. punk band [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] fell apart in Los Angeles, [[Buzz Osborne|9a911b22-f972-44ee-b2d3-d41297fe96e9]] of the Melvins put drummer Grohl in touch with Nirvana. He flew to Seattle, auditioned, and was in.
years.xp: Grohl was in the crowd on September 22 at the Motor Sports International Garage in Seattle for the one show Dan Peters played with Nirvana. He had joined Scream at 17 and toured Europe and the U.S. with them before the band was stranded in L.A. when its bassist left.

years.big: "We knew in two minutes that he was the right drummer"
years.src: Rolling Stone: Dave Grohl · Wikipedia: Nirvana
years.h: Grohl makes his debut at Olympia's North Shore Surf Club
years.p: Novoselic on the audition that came before this first show with Cobain and Novoselic.

eras.title: Number one by accident
eras.text: DGC hoped for 250,000 copies of Nevermind and got a No. 1 album instead. 1992 filled up with Saturday Night Live, a wedding, an argument over publishing and a hospital gown at Reading.

years.h: Nirvana sign to DGC, and Sub Pop takes a cut
years.p: The advance is $287,000 for two albums; Sub Pop gets $75,000 and two percent of the next two records.
years.xp: Those points on Nevermind and Incesticide became a lifeline for Sub Pop, which had been close to broke in 1991.

yt: Smells Like Teen Spirit, official video
years.h: A slogan on a wall becomes Smells Like Teen Spirit
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] wrote on Cobain's wall that he smelled like Teen Spirit. It was the deodorant his girlfriend [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]] wore; Cobain didn't know and heard a slogan.

yt: Smells Like Teen Spirit, live at the Paramount, Seattle, October 31, 1991
years.h: Nevermind starts at No. 144
years.p: DGC ships 46,251 copies to U.S. stores hoping to sell 250,000 in all, about what Sonic Youth's Goo did. By December it's selling hundreds of thousands a week.
years.xp:
[[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] produced at Sound City in Van Nuys in May and June 1991 on a $65,000 budget, and [[Andy Wallace|665695c1-d546-4141-8dd7-1cd40a1eea71]] mixed. Cobain later said: "I'm embarrassed by it now. It's closer to a Mötley Crüe record than punk rock."

On the cover, Kirk Weddle photographed four-month-old Spencer Elden swimming underwater.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain at the Paramount Theatre, Seattle, Halloween 1991
years.h: Michael Jackson loses the top spot to Nevermind
years.p: The Billboard 200 turns over on January 11, 1992, the same day Nirvana play Saturday Night Live. They end the broadcast with Cobain and Novoselic kissing.

years.h: Cobain and Courtney Love marry on a Waikiki beach
years.p: Love fronts [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]]. Their daughter, Frances Bean Cobain, is born that August 18.

years.h: Cobain asks for most of the publishing, backdated to Nevermind
years.p: Novoselic and Grohl agree, and the band survives the argument.
years.xp:
Under the settlement Cobain keeps 75 percent on eleven songs and all of the songs he wrote alone. Novoselic and Grohl get 12.5 percent each on those eleven, including Smells Like Teen Spirit.

That left them living on record, touring and merchandise money while Cobain held most of the publishing.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain at the Reading Festival, August 30, 1992
yt: Smells Like Teen Spirit, Reading Festival, August 30, 1992
years.h: Cobain rolls onstage at Reading in a wheelchair and a wig
years.p: Writer [[Everett True|001897b1-fbb7-4dbe-b1df-ac638bf60afc]] pushes him out in a hospital gown, mocking the rumors about his health, on the last night of the festival. Cobain stands up and plays.

years.h: At the VMAs, Nirvana tease Rape Me and play Lithium
years.p: MTV had refused the song. Novoselic ends the set by throwing his bass in the air and it lands on his head; the band wins Best Alternative Video and Best New Artist.

years.h: Incesticide collects the B-sides and a note from Cobain
years.p: Rarities, BBC sessions and a Dale Crover demo, put out jointly by DGC and Sub Pop to beat the bootleggers. Cobain painted the cover.
years.xp:
Sub Pop owned the old recordings but not Geffen's distribution, so it sold them to Geffen for a six-figure sum, on condition that the album was done by Christmas 1992. It peaked at No. 39 on the Billboard 200.

The liner notes tell anyone who hates homosexuals, people of a different color or women to "leave us the fuck alone!" Cobain is credited as Kurdt Kobain.

eras.title: Louder on record, quieter on TV
eras.text: Nirvana followed Nevermind with In Utero, cut in two weeks with Steve Albini, and a stripped-down MTV set that became their best-loved live document. Cobain was found dead at his Seattle home in April 1994, less than five months after the taping.

years.h: Touch and Go splits a single between Nirvana and the Jesus Lizard
years.p: Nirvana take Oh, the Guilt and [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] take Puss, a nod to the Chicago noise rock Cobain loved.

years.h: Albini turns down royalties and records In Utero in two weeks
years.p: Albini's verdict on producers who take points, before he cuts the album at Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, Minnesota.
years.xp:
Studio fees came to $24,000 and Albini took a flat fee of $100,000, according to Wikipedia. On April 19, 1993 the Chicago Tribune ran Greg Kot's "Record Label Finds Little Bliss in Nirvana's Latest."

Producer Scott Litt remixed Heart-Shaped Box and All Apologies at Bad Animals Studio in Seattle that May. Albini later said: "The record in the stores doesn't sound all that much like the record that was made."

years.h: In Utero opens at No. 1, and Walmart passes
years.p: Walmart and Kmart refuse to stock it. In March 1994 DGC issues a version with the back-cover collage altered and Rape Me listed as Waif Me.
years.xp:
It sold 180,000 copies in its first week. The cover is an anatomical model with angel wings added, and Cobain made the back collage himself.

He called it "the easiest recording we've ever done, hands down."

years.h: Pat Smear of the Germs becomes the second guitarist
years.p: [[Pat Smear|3da65013-dfdd-40c7-b9c7-e4c829862c66]], from L.A. punk band [[Germs|42c4b58d-2e28-41d4-bfe5-4edee68386cf]], joins for the In Utero tour. Nirvana had wanted a second guitarist since Everman.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain and Pat Smear, MTV Unplugged taping, Sony Music Studios, New York, November 1993
yt: The Man Who Sold the World, MTV Unplugged
years.h: Cobain dresses the MTV Unplugged stage with lilies and candles
years.p: Nirvana skip Smells Like Teen Spirit, bring cellist Lori Goldston and Cris and Curt Kirkwood of the [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]], and close with Lead Belly's Where Did You Sleep Last Night.
years.xp:
Cobain asked for stargazer lilies, black candles and a crystal chandelier. The 14 songs were filmed in a single take, and he refused an encore because he couldn't top the closer.

MTV executives were unhappy about the lack of hits and about the Meat Puppets guests, wanting the "right" names.

years.src: Wikipedia: Death of Kurt Cobain · Wikipedia: Nirvana
years.h: Kurt Cobain is found dead at his Seattle home
years.p: An electrician installing security lighting finds him on April 8. The medical examiner puts the death about three days earlier, and Seattle police confirm it as a suicide. He was 27.
years.xp:
Nirvana played what turned out to be their last show on March 1 at Terminal Eins in Munich, and the rest of the European tour was postponed after Cobain was diagnosed with bronchitis and laryngitis. On March 4 he was hospitalized in Rome after an overdose; his management called it accidental, and Courtney Love later described it as a suicide attempt.

In late March he entered a Los Angeles rehab center for heroin addiction and left after less than a week. The band withdrew from Lollapalooza on April 6, and on April 10 about 7,000 people gathered at Seattle Center for a public memorial.

years.h: Seven months later, Unplugged in New York is No. 1
years.p: Released on November 1, it sells 310,500 copies in its first week, the biggest of Nirvana's career, and wins the 1996 Grammy for best alternative music.
years.xp: It has two songs the broadcast left out, Something in the Way and Oh Me. By March 1995 it had outsold In Utero.
play: Where Did You Sleep Last Night

eras.title: A band LLC and one song in a vault
eras.text: Dave Grohl started Foo Fighters and Krist Novoselic went into politics and smaller bands. The catalog they left behind turned into a fight with Courtney Love.

years.h: A settlement frees You Know You're Right
years.p: Courtney Love had blocked a planned box set in 2001 and sued Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl over Nirvana LLC. The 2002 settlement releases the last studio song, on a best-of called Nirvana.
years.xp: The box set followed in November 2004 as With the Lights Out.

eras.title: Guest singers, and the baby goes to court
eras.text: The surviving members kept turning up for one-off sets with guest singers instead of touring as Nirvana. Meanwhile the baby from the Nevermind cover took them to court.

years.h: Four singers take Cobain's place at the Hall of Fame
years.p: At Barclays Center in Brooklyn, [[Joan Jett|f376828a-b438-4fda-bb2e-dcd5fbe81f83]], [[Kim Gordon|19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184]], [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] and Lorde sing in Cobain's place as Nirvana go in, in their first year of eligibility.
years.xp: After the ceremony the surviving members played a late club show at Saint Vitus in Brooklyn with a rotating cast of guests, including [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]].

years.h: FireAid brings Grohl, Novoselic and Smear back together
years.p: They play the L.A. fire relief benefit with guest singers. Two weeks later, on February 14, Post Malone sings Smells Like Teen Spirit with them on SNL's 50th anniversary show.
years.xp: The guests at FireAid were St. Vincent, Kim Gordon, Joan Jett and Violet Grohl. It was the first time the three had played together in five years.

years.h: A judge dismisses the Nevermind baby's lawsuit again
years.p: Spencer Elden sued in 2021, claiming the cover was child pornography. A judge ruled for Nirvana in 2025, and Elden appealed again.
years.xp:
The suit was first dismissed in 2022 and revived by an appeals court in December 2023. Judge Fernando Olguin found the image "most analogous to a family photo of a nude child bathing," and noted that Elden had profited from autographs and from calling himself the "Nirvana baby."

Nirvana's lawyer, Bert Deixler, said: "We will resist with vigor and will prevail." Elden's attorneys filed a new appeal in October 2025.
